newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's controversial Lebed speaks his mind.
newsitem.headline: Russia's controversial Lebed speaks his mind.

text.p: National security adviser Alexander Lebed, visiting NATO in Brussels on Monday in his first trip to a Western country, has been an outspoken and controversial figure since he commanded Russia's 14th Army in Moldova.
He left that job in June 1995 to enter politics and became President Boris Yeltsin's national security adviser a year later.
Lebed's comments are frequently outrageous, often contradictory, but, delivered in a rumbling bass voice, they are rarely dull. Here are some of his statements:
On NATO expansion --

"Some commentators of ill-will have been saying that Lebed is threatening NATO with nuclear weapons, and saying Russia is ready to occupy some of these countries (applying for NATO membership) if there is the slightest move of NATO to the east.
"These are the worst fairy tales of the Cold War." In Brussels in October 1996.

"Let there be no mistake. German and American industrial interests in Russia will suffer directly as a result of (NATO) enlargement plans". To Britain's Daily Telegraph in September 1996. Lebed's office later denied the comments had been made.
NATO acts like "a big drunken hooligan in a kindergarten who says he will hit anyone he likes". October 1995.
If NATO begins expanding through Eastern Europe, "World War Three will start. Civilised and uncivilised states will be destroyed, everybody and everything." April 1995.
On Chechnya and the Russian army --
"Russia does not have a historical tradition of military coups. Thank God we are not Argentina." Sept 1996.

On Chechnya's capital, Grozny -- "Here we have a Russian city, bombed to bits by Russian planes paid for by Russian taxpayers who are now going to have to pay a second time to rebuild it." October 1995.

On Chechnya -- "Unprepared, untrained boys have been thrown to face bullets. It is a criminal power that sends hundreds of its citizens to certain death... The president of Russia should tender his resignation." February 1995.
On politics --
"What kind of an election is it, if there is no fraud?" June 1996, as presidential candidate before the June election.
"If you need to change the constitution, you should change the constitution," June 1996, on forming a coalition government to rule Russia.
On governing -- "If you bang your fist down once on the desk...the question is closed." July 1994.
"I'm not one to praise Pinochet... but he saved the state from total collapse... The loudmouths were forced, and forced in a brutal manner, to shut their mouths." July 1994.
On culture and religion --
"All these Mormons are mould and filth which have come to destroy the state. The state should outlaw them." June 1996, commenting on evangelical Mormons in Russia.

"I am against anyone teaching us how to live here. I would like to see the Americans' reaction if Russian Orthodox Old Believers landed in Alabama and started teaching them how to live and what to believe." June 1996
" Western cultural expansion is one of the central issues of Russia's national security." June 1996.
On rivals and colleagues --
President Boris Yeltsin -- "A minus" July 1994.
Ultranationalist Vladimir Zhirinovsky -- "The Lord God's monkey." October 1995.
Former defence minister Pavel Grachev -- "I don't like prostitutes, whether they are wearing a skirt or trousers." October 1995
On his own future --
"I was a born winner. Sooner or later, victory will be mine." June 1996.
